drafted_from: tool:install-a-tool-source's row in tool-rows.json, do-work/install-a-tool-source.mjs and test/install-a-tool-source.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Add my team's tools to all my computers: the archive at https://git.example.net/team/tools/-/archive/<commit>/tools.tar.gz, pinned by its files." It adds a row to your tool sources, and each of your computers installs it on its own.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: your tool sources are rows in your own database, and this installs what one row says on the computer it runs on.
instructions: 1. Keep one row per tool source in your own database: its label, the https address of a gzip tar archive of its tool folders, and files_blake3, the pin of its files (node tools/workflows/do-work/pin-a-commit-by-its-files.mjs REPOSITORY COMMIT ADDRESS prints both).
2. Switch on the workflow that runs this tool when a row of that table changes, on each computer of yours. Switching it on grants the right to install any of your sources.
3. Add, change or remove a row. Each computer installs it (or takes it away) by itself and answers changed, files_blake3 and previous; a computer that was off catches up when it is back.

worked_examples.title: A teammate's tool source on every computer
worked_examples.ask: Install my team's tools on this computer: label team-tools, the archive https://archive.example.test/team/tools.tar.gz, pin bbbb...bbbb.
worked_examples.given: From test/install-a-tool-source.test.mjs, with a stub door: the tool sends tools:update to @tools with {source: "team-tools", address, files_blake3} under the key install-a-tool-source:team-tools:<pin>, and the stub answers {changed: true, files_blake3, previous: null}.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"source":"team-tools","changed":true,"files_blake3":"bbbb...bbbb","previous":null}. The same row again answers changed false; {source, removed: true} answers removed true.
